propositions: A pure prepacked single-pass verifier produces false-positive rejections when the prepack is imperfect; a hybrid approach using prepacked evidence only to PASS/ABSTAIN per criterion (never REJECT), with fallback to agentic verification for abstained ACs, eliminates false-positive rejection by construction.

The filter+fallback design achieves -26% token cost overall and -46% on all-met tickets vs pure-agentic verification, with filter cost negligible (~0.4% of agentic spend), while maintaining zero false-positive passes on adversarial test variants.

Filter coverage is bimodal by AC style: ACs naming greppable artifacts (tests, symbols, files) achieve 80-90% pass rate from static packs; ACs asserting runtime outcomes or store-side artifacts rationally abstain, yielding 0-40% coverage depending on ticket composition.

The verify_completion deterministic 8000-char description admission cap must be re-checked after AC-block reduction in any productized implementation; adversarial edits must be length-neutral to avoid spurious fast-fails.

Agentic verifier false-fail variance (2/7 genuine ACs failed alongside planted unmet ones in one run) persists in the fallback but is narrowed by the filter; cost comparisons between filter+fallback and pure-agentic show ±30% single-run variance on identical criteria sets.
